g.text: beats/min; beats
Tempo tells how fast beats pass. Beat position says
where we are in the song; tempo may change there.

g.text: beats/bar; ticks/beat
How many beats make a bar, and how many ticks
divide a beat. This system uses m = r = 4.

g.text: beats or bars; h = mL
How far ahead stage v is asked to work. Writing and
audio can have different leads; this is not ready audio.

g.text: ticks
How early before playback the bar choice is frozen.
The usual whole-bar cutoff is one tick early.

g.text: ms
Time set aside after stage v for later steps and safety.
Include the guard here once; do not add it twice.

g.text: seconds
Maps a beat position to a clock time using the tempo
at each beat. T0 is the session start in seconds.

g.text: How long this stage has after release.
A negative value means already too late.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #2f6bdb

g.text: WHY ONE GROUP?
They turn musical distance into clock time. Two bars of lead mean different seconds at different tempos;
a deadline also needs a named stage, its release time and the time reserved afterward.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #2f6bdb

g.text: EXAMPLE / CONSTANT 90 BPM
Two-bar lead = 5.333 s.
One-tick guard = 0.167 s.
Finish cutoff = 5.167 s after release.
release
0 s
cutoff
play
